speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. You've mentioned increasing pain and swelling in your left knee for the past two months; to help me understand the cause, how would you describe the nature of this pain, and what activities seem to make it worse or better?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the severe pain that awakens you from sleep and the lack of response to NSAIDs, I need to determine if this is inflammatory or mechanical in origin. Does the knee feel warm or red to the touch, and have you noticed any stiffness when first getting out of bed in the morning? Also, have you experienced any fever, chills, or a recent injury to the leg?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe pain and swelling in the left knee. I also have Pain intensifying over 2 months, Painful awakenings during night, No relief with ibuprofen. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pseudogout (Calcium Pyrophosphate Deposition Disease)

The previous suggestion of a urinary tract infection is unrelated to your knee symptoms; to confirm my suspicion of crystal arthropathy, I need to see your joint fluid analysis. REQUEST TEST: Synovial_Fluid_Analysis_for_Crystals. REQUEST IMAGES: Left_Knee_XRay.
